findings.title: Species-level detection mostly survives
findings.text: Mean class AUC 98.7 on focal vs 93.0 on soundscape (out of 100); 12 of 14 species keep AUC ≥ 90 on soundscapes. foxspa collapses (AUC drops by 32 points).

evidence.method: Class ROC-AUC of the model's sigmoid output for the species, on the focal clips (negatives = other species) and the 8,400 soundscape clips.

findings.title: Prototypes transfer unevenly
findings.text: 30 of 70 prototypes lose more than 10 points of detection AUC on soundscapes while 6 improve; in 8 of 14 species the best- and worst-transferring prototypes differ by at least 15 points of AUC.

evidence.method: ΔAUC = soundscape − focal ROC-AUC of each prototype's max activation as a detector of its own species. Spread = max − min ΔAUC among a species' prototypes.

findings.title: Activations shrink, ranking survives
findings.text: On clips with the species, the median soundscape activation is 42% of the focal one (pooled medians 27 → 10 out of 100). On clips without it, activations stay near zero (83% are 5 or less), so positives still rank above negatives: median prototype AUC on soundscapes is 87.

evidence.method: Each entry is one prototype's max activation on one clip, pooled over the 70 prototypes of the analysed species. Positives = clips labelled with the prototype's species. n = focal_pos 12,325, focal_neg 288,885, soundscape_pos 22,110, soundscape_neg 565,890.

findings.title: Evidence shares are stable, but the top prototype often changes
findings.text: Each prototype's share of the class evidence correlates across domains (r = 0.83, mean change 4.7 points), yet the top prototype is the same in only 5 of 14 species. Largest shifts: foxspa P1 20%→38%, yerwar P5 26%→13%, whcspa P3 18%→31%.

stats: Species with the same top prototype
evidence.method: Share = mean over positive clips of w_k·a_k / Σ_j w_j·a_j (w = non-negative last-layer weight, a = max activation): the fraction of the class logit (minus bias) from prototype k.

findings.title: Some failing prototypes simply go silent
findings.text: 10 of 30 failing prototypes (ΔAUC below −10 points) have zero activation on more than 25% of the soundscape clips that contain their species, against 1 of the other 40. Only 5 failing prototypes are silent on more than half, so silence accounts for part of the failures, not most. Counting only clips where a prototype fires, the number whose typical peak moves from above 1 kHz on focal clips to below 0.5 kHz on soundscapes is 1 of 70 (clanut P5).

stats: Failing prototypes silent on > 25% of soundscape positives
daejun P2 silent on positives, focal → soundscape
whcspa P1 silent on positives, focal → soundscape
whcspa P5 silent on positives, focal → soundscape
evidence.method: Silent = the prototype's max activation on a clip is exactly zero (activations pass through a ReLU). Shares are over clips labelled with the species. The link with failing is partly built in: a silent positive ties with every silent negative, which lowers AUC. Peak frequency is taken only over clips where the prototype is active.

findings.title: False matches are often other birds, not noise
findings.text: Among each prototype's top 20 soundscape false matches, a median of 85% contain another annotated species, vs 45% of all clips without the species; 64 of 70 prototypes are enriched by > 10 points. 48 prototypes concentrate on one other species, e.g. mouchi P5 → amerob (18/20 top false matches vs a 1% base rate).

stats: Median share of top-20 false matches with another species
Median base rate (all clips without the species)
Prototypes concentrating on one species (≥ 30% of top matches, ≥ 2× base)
evidence.method: For each prototype, its 20 highest-activating soundscape clips not labelled with its species. 'Contains another species' uses the BirdSet HSN multi-label annotations (21 species). Base rate = fraction of all soundscape clips without the species that contain the other species (or any species). Caveats: some top 'false' matches may be unannotated calls of the species itself, and any bird vocalisation resembles a prototype more than silence does, so enrichment for 'any species' is partly expected; concentration on one specific species is the stronger signal of confusion.

findings.title: Some prototypes match the same acoustic part in both domains
findings.text: whcspa P3 (a pure-tone note) and P4 (a series of falling sweeps) mostly fire on the same kind of structure in focal and soundscape clips, with soundscape AUC 94 and 92 (out of 100). P5's best soundscape matches also resemble its focal ones, but it is usually silent: median soundscape activation 0 on clips with the species, and AUC 69.

evidence.method: Visual inspection of the top-3 activating patches per domain (crop = peak cell ± 2 grid cells), checked against each prototype's AUC and median activation on all positive clips (table).

findings.title: Top matches can look different across domains
findings.text: Two of whcspa P2's three top focal matches are sharp rising sweeps; all three top soundscape matches are a buzz-like band near 6 kHz, which resembles the buzz in the third focal match. The images cannot show whether these are song or noise. Its soundscape AUC is 92.

evidence.method: Visual inspection of the top-3 activating patches per domain, without listening to the audio. Three examples per domain say nothing about how common each kind of match is.

caveats: Focal clips are Xeno-Canto recordings, which are part of the model's XCL training data: focal numbers are an in-domain reference, not a held-out score.
Species with fewer than 30 soundscape positives have noisy soundscape statistics.
Prototype AUC uses the prototype's max activation as a detector of its own species (focal negatives = other species' focal clips; soundscape negatives = all other soundscape clips).
